result.title: Preface
result.summary:
BOSTON RETIREMENT SYSTEM (“BRS”)
INVESTMENT CONSULTING SERVICES REQUEST FOR PROPOSALS (“RFP”)

result.title: TIMELINE
result.summary: The text gives the Boston Retirement System investment consulting RFP timeline: issued February 7, 2022; written questions due February 18; BRS responses February 25; proposals due March 1; presentations, visits, and finalist selection April 1–May 2; consultant selected May 18. BRS may amend the schedule. Proposals must arrive by 4:00 p.m. EST on March 1 and include seven printed copies and one electronic copy. Printed proposals go to the Boston Retirement Board, Boston City Hall, Room 816, Boston, MA 02201, attention John F. Kelly, Investment Analyst, marked “Mail Room – Do Not Open RFP Response”; the electronic version goes to john.kelly@boston.gov. The contents list the introduction, service summary and scope, minimum qualifications, proposal terms and conditions, evaluation process, and four attachments: required-attachment checklist, minimum-qualification certification, investment consultant proposal questionnaire, and prospective consultant certification sheet.

result.title: I INTRODUCTION
result.summary: The Boston Retirement System (BRS) is a Chapter 32 cost-sharing, multi-employer public retirement system and member of the Massachusetts Contributory Retirement System. Its five-member Board comprises the City Auditor, two elected members, a Mayor-appointed member, and a fifth member selected by the other four. Current members are Maureen Joyce (ex officio; indefinite term), Daniel J. Greene (appointed chair; term ends 3/13/23), Michael W. McLaughlin (elected; 9/30/23), Michael D. O’Reilly (elected; 9/30/23), and Thomas V.J. Jackson (fifth member; 1/15/24). The Board meets monthly, records proceedings, annually submits expense estimates and financial statements to PERAC, and approves retirement allowances for PERAC verification. The Executive Officer oversees daily operations and about 52 City Hall staff, who handle member and retiree contact. Statements follow PERAC practices substantially aligned with GAAP, though requirements differ; records use a calendar year, and the Investment Income Account receives accrued and received interest and dividends. The Board controls external investment decisions, with manager recommendations at monthly meetings. Portfolio value is about $6.7 billion, plus $2.2 billion in PRIT; assets under management are reported as of December 31, 2021.

result.title: BRS INVESTMENT PORTFOLIO ASSETS UNDER MANAGEMENT
result.summary: As of December 31, 2021, BRS’s unaudited portfolio totaled $6.77 billion across U.S. and non-U.S. equities, public fixed income, hedge funds, real estate, private equity, and cash. BRS sought a general investment consultant for a five-year term, with two optional one-year extensions. Services include annual policy and asset-allocation reviews; public-portfolio, manager, performance, risk, fee, trading-cost, and commission-recapture analysis; manager searches and oversight; Board education and meeting support; and private-market investment, manager, valuation, performance, fee, strategy, and search advice, coordinated with the existing private-equity discretionary manager. Firms must meet minimum experience qualifications. Proposal rules specify deadlines, delivery format, fees, public-record status, authorized signatures, addenda, restrictions on contact and publicity, and sealed opening. BRS evaluates compliant proposals for qualifications, fit, capabilities, experience, value, and other factors, using screening, written and comparative ratings, possible interviews and site visits, and Board selection.

nodes.title: II SUMMARY OF SERVICES
nodes.summary: BRS’s unaudited investment portfolio totaled $6,769,451,298 as of December 31, 2021: U.S. equity, $1,738,929,474; non-U.S. equity (international and emerging), $1,663,096,490; public fixed income (core, high yield, global), $1,726,859,697; hedge funds, $311,126,638; real estate, $584,685,755; private equity, $668,147,714; and cash, $76,605,530. BRS seeks proposals from qualified firms for general investment consulting, including asset allocation, risk management, public markets, private real estate, private equity/debt, and hedge fund or other alternatives consulting; further details appear in Section III, Scope of Services. The selected consultant’s agreement will run for five years, with options for two additional one-year extensions.

nodes.title: III SCOPE OF SERVICES
nodes.summary: The consultant will advise BRS and its Board/staff on general, public-market, and private-market investments. General services include reviewing investment policies annually; preparing a comprehensive asset-allocation plan using PERAC actuarial analysis and annual optimization reports; and providing requested research and operational advice. Public-market work covers annual portfolio and manager reviews, quarterly portfolio performance, attribution, style, risk and fee analysis, and semiannual manager evaluations. It also includes manager oversight advice, probation/termination recommendations, and annual commission-recapture and trading-cost analysis. The consultant will support manager searches (assume four annually), maintain manager information, develop RFPs, screen and interview candidates, rank them on PERAC’s 1–4 scale, and advise on selection. Board-meeting attendance and requested investment education are also required. For private markets—private equity, debt and real estate—the consultant will assess existing investments, managers and fees and recommend portfolio assets, future strategy and fee policy; provide quarterly valuation, performance and fee reporting; and support searches (assume four annually) through manager databases, RFPs, screening, interviews, rankings and selection advice, coordinating with BRS’s current private-equity discretionary manager.

nodes.title: IV MINIMUM QUALIFICATIONS
nodes.summary:
IV MINIMUM QUALIFICATIONS
Prospective Consultants must meet the minimum qualifications as listed in Attachment 2 (Minimum Qualification Certification). Does the Prospective Consultant firm have at least three (3) years of experience performing substantially similar services for institutional clients? Does the prospective “lead Consultant” on the BRS account have at least five (5) years of experience advising systems of similar size and scope to BRS

nodes.title: V TERMS AND CONDITIONS FOR SUBMITTING PROPOSALS
nodes.summary: The RFP sets a February 18, 2022, 4:00 p.m. EST deadline for emailed questions to BRS; questions and responses will be emailed to RFP recipients on February 25 without identifying questioners. Late proposals are disqualified at the proposer’s risk. BRS may reject proposals or waive irregularities; the RFP is not a contract, and proposals become public records after the deadline. Fees must follow Attachment 3’s format and may be negotiated downward, never upward. Submit seven printed copies and one electronic copy; the signed, labeled Master Copy must be in a three-ring binder, with proposals delivered as directed. Submissions become BRS property, and noncompliance may result in rejection. BRS may issue emailed addenda; proposers must promptly report errors. Publicity about BRS or a resulting contract requires prior written approval. An authorized person must sign Attachment 4 and state their title. From February 7, proposers may not contact BRS staff or board members about the RFP except through written questions; existing business contacts are limited to that business. Sealed proposals will be opened in closed session with witnesses on March 2 at 1:00 p.m. EDT.

nodes.title: VI. EVALUATION PROCESS
key_items: 11. The Board will make the final Consultant(s) selection.
nodes.summary: BRS will evaluate proposals for organizational fit, alignment of interests, value, resources, capabilities, firm and assigned staff experience, clarity, demonstrated insight, and other relevant factors, and may request clarifications. Evaluation will impartially assess minimum qualifications and identify consultants most likely to perform successfully. Proposals must meet submission requirements and minimum criteria; failures are eliminated. BRS may waive or permit correction of minor, non-prejudicial informalities. If an obvious mistake and intended offer are evident, BRS will correct it and notify the consultant in writing; the proposal cannot be withdrawn, and no other changes will be made. Qualifying proposals receive written evaluations using the RFP evaluation form, criterion ratings, and composite ratings with explanations. The most advantageous responsible and responsive proposal is selected based on price and criteria through minimum screening, comparative evaluation, composite ratings, and final selection. BRS staff and/or Board may conduct finalist office due diligence and interviews; on-site visits were planned for April 2022. The Board makes the final selection.

result.title: Investment Consulting Services BRS Investment Consultant Search
result.summary: A Board and staff proposal evaluation form for the BRS investment consultant search, with fields for proposing firm, evaluator, and review date. It scores proposals from Highly Advantageous (10 points), Advantageous (7), Acceptable (5), Not Advantageous (2), to Unacceptable (0) across ten criteria: firm stability and experience; consultant-team stability and experience; corporate structure, scale, scope, conflicts, and ethics; client investment outcomes; strategy development, pacing model, philosophy, research, processes, and insights; risk philosophy and management or mitigation; manager-database scale and scope, ratings, due diligence, and hiring/firing philosophy; firm research, Board education, and other relevant factors; consultant-team perspectives, impression, and ability to relate to the Board; and value for the Board’s needs at a reasonable price.
